title: How to Create Web APIs in ASP.NET Core [.NET 8.0 LTS RESTful pattern]
description: Build a fully functional RESTful Web API in ASP.NET Core using controllers, attribute routing, and JSON serialization.

data.text: What Is a Web API?

A **Web API** is an interface that other applications can call over the internet using standard **HTTP** protocols. Unlike a traditional MVC controller that returns HTML views, a Web API controller returns **data** — usually as JSON. This makes it perfect for serving mobile apps, SPAs, or any client that needs structured data.

data.caption: A Web API sits between clients and data, returning JSON over HTTP.
data.definition:
graph LR
    A[Mobile App] -->|GET /api/Reservation| S[Web API Server]
    B[SPA / JavaScript] -->|POST /api/Reservation| S
    C[PowerShell Script] -->|GET /api/Reservation/1| S
    D[Another Service] -->|DELETE /api/Reservation/3| S
    S --> E[(In-Memory Repository)]
    S -->|JSON Response| A
    S -->|JSON Response| B
    S -->|JSON Response| C
    S -->|204 No Content| D

data.text: REST — The Design Pattern Behind Web APIs

**REST** stands for **REpresentational State Transfer**. It is an architectural style that gives rules for how a Web API should behave. A RESTful API uses standard HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) on **resource-based URLs** like `/api/Reservation` instead of action-based URLs like `/getAllReservations`.

terms.definition: Any entity the API manages — a Reservation, Product, or Order. Resources are addressed by nouns in the URL.
The method of a request — GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE — that describes the intended action.
Each request contains all the information needed. The server does not store client context between requests.
JavaScript Object Notation — the lightweight text format used to exchange data with Web APIs.

data.text: ControllerBase vs Controller

Web API controllers in ASP.NET Core must derive from **`ControllerBase`**, not `Controller`. `ControllerBase` provides HTTP-specific helpers (like `Ok()`, `BadRequest()`, `NotFound()`) without the overhead of view-related features. Use `Controller` only when the same class serves both views and APIs.

cards.title: ControllerBase
cards.description: Base class for API controllers. Provides HTTP helpers only.

cards.title: Controller
cards.description: Full controller inheriting from ControllerBase. Adds View support.
pros: Can return Views and API results
cons: Not recommended for dedicated API controllers

data.text: How Routing Works

The route template `[Route("api/[controller]")]` uses a **route token** (`[controller]`) that ASP.NET Core replaces with the controller name minus the "Controller" suffix. So `ReservationController` maps to `/api/Reservation`.

data.caption: How the route template resolves to actual URLs for each HTTP verb.
data.definition:
graph LR
    RT["[Route(api/[controller])]"] -->|controller = Reservation| BASE[/api/Reservation]
    BASE -->|GET [HttpGet]| G1[GET /api/Reservation → all records]
    BASE -->|GET + id [HttpGet("{id}")]| G2[GET /api/Reservation/1 → one record]
    BASE -->|POST [HttpPost]| P1[POST /api/Reservation → create]
    BASE -->|PUT [HttpPut]| PU1[PUT /api/Reservation → update]
    BASE -->|PATCH + id [HttpPatch("{id}")]| PA1[PATCH /api/Reservation/1 → partial update]
    BASE -->|DELETE + id [HttpDelete("{id}")]| D1[DELETE /api/Reservation/1 → delete]

Testing the API

Run the project and navigate directly to `https://localhost:<port>/api/Reservation` in your browser. Because it is a GET request, the browser will display the raw JSON response without needing any client code.

data.title: Content-Type header
data.text: ASP.NET Core automatically sets the response Content-Type to application/json for any non-string return type. You do not need to set it manually in action methods.
[ApiController] Attribute Behaviors
The `[ApiController]` attribute enables several automatic behaviors that simplify API development:

data.title: Automatic behaviors from [ApiController]
items: **Attribute routing** is required — route templates are applied automatically.
**400 Bad Request** is returned automatically when model binding fails — no need to manually validate every parameter.
**Binding source inference** — the framework infers `[FromBody]`, `[FromRoute]`, and `[FromQuery]` based on parameter type.
**Multipart/form-data** is inferred when `[FromForm]` is present on a parameter.
**ProblemDetails** responses follow RFC 7807 for consistent error formatting across APIs.

items.question: Why not use Controller instead of ControllerBase for APIs?
items.answer: ControllerBase is lighter because it excludes view-related features. Using ControllerBase makes your intent clear — this class is for APIs only.

items.question: What is [FromBody] and when do I need it?
items.answer: [FromBody] tells ASP.NET Core to read the parameter from the HTTP request body. It is required for complex types sent as JSON in POST and PATCH actions.

items.question: Why does my PATCH action need Newtonsoft.Json?
items.answer: JsonPatchDocument<T> is provided by the Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch package, which is built on Newtonsoft.Json. System.Text.Json does not yet support JSON Patch.

items.question: Where does the data go when the app restarts?
items.answer: The Dictionary-based repository is in-memory only. All data is lost when the process stops. Replace it with a database context (e.g. Entity Framework Core) for persistence.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: A Web API controller derives from ControllerBase and is decorated with [ApiController].
REST maps CRUD operations to standard HTTP verbs on resource URLs like /api/Reservation.
The repository pattern separates data logic from controller logic, making the API easier to test and maintain.
ASP.NET Core automatically serializes return values to JSON — no manual serialization needed in action methods.
Register services with AddSingleton in Program.cs to make them available via dependency injection.
data.takeaway: You now have a working RESTful Web API. The next step is to test every endpoint and then learn how to consume it from client code.
